relevance.rationale: An expository survey on the edge of algebra, logic and geometry: universal algebraic geometry over algebraic systems and logical rigidity (Sec. 2.1), Plotkin's problem on Aut(End(W(X))) for free commutative/associative algebras (Sec. 2.2), nonstandard analysis (ultraproducts at an infinite prime) applied to the Belov-Kontsevich isomorphism and to Plotkin's conjecture for polynomial symplectomorphisms (Sec. 2.3), a universal Turing machine realised inside a finitely presented algebra so that nilpotency and zero-divisor problems become undecidable (Sec. 3.1), and undecidability of the embeddability problem for varieties over a characteristic-zero field via a Matiyasevich family (Sec. 3.2). Measured against what the folio needs, it supplies nothing: a full-text search finds zero occurrences of Hecke, Temperley-Lieb, Young/partition diagram, Catalan, Wenzl, meander, Gram determinant, Connes, Rieffel, Lip-norm, Kantorovich, deuteron/nuclear, Kashaev, dilogarithm or hyperbolic volume; the two 'Markov' hits are A. A. Markov's 1947 word-problem paper and an author name, not the Markov trace. Two adjacencies were checked and both fail to be load-bearing. (a) The folio's unital-Groebner-bases chapter is about UNITAL GS bases over an arbitrary commutative ground ring; Sec. 3.1 works over a field and is about algorithmic undecidability, not ground-ring generality or PBW, and the chapter's existing citations already cover the background. (b) The information-theory chapter (rem:skein-turing-machine, thm:geometry-of-incompleteness, prop:incompleteness-implies-horizon) asserts a Turing-complete braid/Skein substrate, and Thms 3.1-3.2 are a genuine algebraic instance of computation embedded in an algebra -- but the folio makes no claim about the decidability of any algebraic property of a presented algebra, so no block wants it, and this document explicitly defers those proofs ('The entire proofs can be found at [29]') to Ivanov-Pogodaev and Malev, J. Algebra 508 (2018) 575-588, which is what should be cited if that fact is ever wanted. Scope-(a) negative: as read, it supplies nothing usable here; that is not a claim that model-theoretic or undecidability methods are irrelevant to the folio in principle.

proposedActions.rationale: Nearest live hook checked: rem:skein-turing-machine encodes a Turing machine as a braid and carries no citations, and Sec. 3.1's Thms 3.1-3.2 are the closest external analogue in the corpus. But the remark claims computation-in-a-braid, not undecidability of an algebraic property, so nothing there is unsourced; and this is a survey that defers the proofs to a different paper. Citing it would register a bibliography entry whose load-bearing content lives elsewhere.

Second hook checked: the unital-Groebner-bases chapter. Sec. 3.1's noncommutative Groebner-basis material is over a field and about undecidability; it does not touch the arbitrary-commutative-ground-ring generality that thm:unital-groebner-decomposition and cor:pbw assert, which leitnerpawloski2004 already sources.
